about.title: El Monte Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Five people died on El Monte's streets in 2025, according to the most recent final crash data for the city. Each of those numbers was a parent, a partner, someone whose absence is still felt at a kitchen table somewhere between Valley Boulevard and Lower Azusa Road. A wrongful death claim is the civil process California gives surviving family members to hold a careless driver, property owner, or business accountable for that loss. It runs separately from any criminal case and can proceed whether or not charges are filed. Under state law, a spouse or domestic partner and children have the first right to bring the claim, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks when a public agency is involved, such as a claim tied to a city-maintained road or a Caltrans stretch of the I-10. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect El Monte families with an independent wrongful death attorney who works on contingency; the introduction is free.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on the I-10 in El Monte and the driver is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, the two proceed on separate tracks. The criminal case is brought by the Los Angeles County District Attorney and focuses on punishment, not on compensating your family. A wrongful death claim is the civil action that addresses funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. It can move forward regardless of how the criminal case ends.

items.question: What can our family actually recover in a California wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Recoverable losses generally include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Each family's situation is different, so no one can responsibly predict a figure up front. An attorney will look at your specific circumstances and explain what applies.
